QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_3

question.text: Garuda Growth Fund (Cat II) has called INR 1,000 cr of committed capital. Total distributions to date equal INR 2,500 cr. PPM waterfall: (i) Return of Capital, (ii) 8% preferred return computed on called capital (for simplicity, 1 year holding), (iii) 100% GP catch-up, (iv) 80/20 profit split thereafter. Ignoring fund expenses, what is the GP's CARRY entitlement?

explanation.text: The Logic: Step 1: Return capital — LP gets 1,000. Remaining pool = 1,500. Step 2: Pref return 8% on 1,000 = 80 to LP. Remaining = 1,420. Step 3: 100% catch-up to GP until GP has received 20% of (Pref + Catch-up). Let catch-up = C; solve C = 0.20 * (80 + C) => 0.80 C = 16 => C = 20. Remaining = 1,400. Step 4: 80/20 split of 1,400 => LP 1,120, GP 280. Total GP carry = 20 (catch-up) + 280 (80/20) = INR 300 cr. Total distribution check: LP 1,000 + 80 + 1,120 = 2,200; GP 20 + 280 = 300; sum = 2,500. Correct. The Trap: INR 284 cr comes from forgetting the 100% catch-up and simply taking 20% of (2,500 - 1,000 - 80) = 284 — a classic American-vs-European blend error. INR 200 cr is 20% of catch-up-less profit after pref. INR 320 cr double-counts the catch-up into the 20% line.
